James (Support): FYI customer reported their Dedicated pool didn't scale during a traffic spike; they saw ~30s tail latency and intermittent 429s. attaching logs and repro from the session.
Maria (Eng-runtime): Can you paste the request ids or a small window of logs? Is this a new Dedicated tenant or existing? any prod change recently?
James (Support): Tenant: acme-marketing-prod. No config change on their side. Request ids: req=acm-9a2f, acm-9a31. From their trace: 2024-11-05T14:03:12Z spike, probes fired but no new replica till ~14:04:05Z.
James (Support): Snippet they shared:
```
2024-11-05T14:03:12.123Z GET /v1/gen 200 latency=230ms pool_capacity=8 inflight=48 queued=22
2024-11-05T14:03:20.456Z autoscaler: evaluate -> need +4 but backoff_active=true
2024-11-05T14:04:05.789Z provisioner: new replica registered
```
Kevin (Eng-SRE): Got it. That backoff flag is interesting. We rolled an autoscaler change yesterday to add a 30s scaling cooldown when preflight failures occur. Might be suppressing reactive scaleup in presence of probe flaps.
Maria (Eng-runtime): Also check min_replicas and max_replicas on that tenant. If min is low and burst >> batch size, you'll see queueing while instances cold-start. James, can you confirm their min/max config?
James (Support): Their config: min_replicas=2, max_replicas=20, burst_reserve=0. They are using g5x2 pool. No warm pool enabled explicitly.
Sophie (Customer Success): Customer says this impacts an email send job at ~14:00, they retried and got success once scaled. They're asking for mitigation and whether we can guarantee warm instances for scheduled jobs.
Maria (Eng-runtime): Short-term mitigation: increase min_replicas to 6 or enable warm_pool (prewarmed replicas) for scheduled heavy jobs. Long-term: we should revisit the cooldown logic and how probe flaps mark backoff_active.
Kevin (Eng-SRE): I'll pull the autoscaler logs for that tenant (node labels) and check for noisy-neighbor indicators. Also check cloud provider quota events; sometimes instance provisioning stalls due to AZ capacity. infra-bot, can you check recent quota/placement errors for g5x2 in us-west-2?
infra-bot: Checked provider telemetry 14:00-14:05 UTC: 3 placement failures in us-west-2a; no hard quota limits hit. Notable: one host reported OOM eviction events across a different tenant 13:58-14:01.
Maria (Eng-runtime): OOM evictions elsewhere could cause noisy neighbor slowdowns; but placement failures + cooldown could explain the 40s wall time before replica came up.
James (Support): Customer asked for a timeline and root cause. I'll draft an update: we're investigating autoscaler cooldown interactions + cloud placement noise; recommended temp change: bump min_replicas to 6 and enable warm_pool for their scheduled ramp.
Kevin (Eng-SRE): Action items:
- [ ] I will collect autoscaler debug trace for tenant acme-marketing-prod (investigating backoff flag footprint)
- [ ] infra to raise placement telemetry ticket with provider if placement failures > 5 in 1h
- [ ] Suggest product consider a "scheduled warm pool" feature for recurring jobs
oncall-bot: Assigned @Kevin (Eng-SRE) as owner for this thread. Escalation level: P2. ETA for initial root-cause: 4h.
Maria (Eng-runtime): Quick note: there's a config flag `scale_holdoff_ms` we introduced last week; if set per-tenant it can prevent back-to-back scale actions. Kevin, check if acme has an override.
Kevin (Eng-SRE): I see acme has no override, it's using default 30000ms. I'll pull traces and post back within the hour.
James (Support): Thanks. I'll tell the customer the short-term mitigation and that we have an SRE owner. :thumbsup:
